keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The Dutch Malacca page describes the town and its fortress (A Famosa) and harbour only, 'Area: not given', and does not mention Naning, Rembau or Sungai Ujong, so the outline is the Portuguese-period city. The British held the town from January 1795 to 1818 (ledger occupation pair), the Dutch governors of 1818-1825 are in the page's table.

ledger.note: January 1641: the Dutch take Malacca. The page: the Dutch 'assaulted and wrested Malacca from the Portuguese in January 1641' (infobox 'Established: 14 January 1641'); 'As per the agreement with Johor in 1606, the Dutch took control of Malacca', and Johor supplied 'around 500-600 additional men'.

ledger.note: January 1795: the British occupy Malacca. 'Malacca was thus surrendered to British control' in January 1795, following the Kew Letters (infobox 'British occupation: 1795-1818'); Willem Jacob Cranssen is listed as Dutch governor in 1802 within the British residents' table. [Reviewer se-03-x, 2026-10-24: month removed: the Dutch Malacca page dates the Kew Letters to January 1795 and says only that Malacca 'was thus surrendered to British control', with no month for the surrender]

ledger.note: 1818: the Dutch regain Malacca. 'The Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1814 restored Malacca to Dutch rule,' but the Dutch 'did not regain full control until 1818' (infobox 'British occupation: 1795-1818'; governor Thijssen 1818-1822).

1818: Malacca returns as part of the Dutch East Indies. Infobox status: 'Colony of the Dutch East India Company (1641-1795); part of the Dutch East Indies (1818-1825)'. The change of status is the page's; no dossier of the Dutch East Indies of that period records Malacca.

ledger.note: 1 March 1825: Malacca passes to Britain. 'The Netherlands ceded the city and fort of Malacca' (Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824, signed 17 March 1824 by Fagel and Canning); 'All transfers of property and establishments were to take place on 1 March 1825'. Britain ceded Fort Marlborough at Bencoolen and its Sumatran possessions in exchange.

notes: Written 2026-10-24 by the se-03-x additions batch. A colony Cliopatria lacks (the town sits inside the Sultanate of Malacca and British shapes). Two pages opened (the page budget for a state with no shapes is 2-5). Unsettled: (1) the page gives no area or hinterland (Naning, Rembau, Sungai Ujong are not on it); the outline is the town; (2) the 1795-1818 British occupation is recorded in the owner's ledger with the occupier as counterpart (the dutch-east-indies convention); british-colonial-empire should carry the mirror occupation_start/end and the 1825 gain; (3) 'rename' in 1818 is a status caption (VOC colony to part of the Dutch East Indies), not a new name; (4) 1 March 1825 is the transfer date, the Straits Settlements dossier starts in 1826, so Malacca is British between: the successors line names straits-settlements as the page does; (5) the Naning War (1831), the Kota Supai fort (1757) and the Johor-Dutch treaties are not on the pages opened.
